CHOICE: 2
CONFIDENCE: 3

Solution 1 is wrong because the inclusion $S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp))\subset S_k(\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r))$ only gives a lower bound. It does not show the multiplicity stays fixed as $r$ grows.

Solution 3 is not supported. Its index-based heuristic is not a valid argument for the multiplicity, and its exponent is hedged rather than derived.

Solution 2 matches the classical analogue. In the classical setting, a form of level $M$ occurs in level $N$ with multiplicity equal to the number of divisors of $N/M$. Here $N/M = p^{r-1}$ for $M=p$, which gives $r$ choices. I believe the Drinfeld-setting result (Hattori and related work on finite-slope forms of level $\Gamma_1(\mathfrak n\wp^r)$) has the same linear form, but I could not verify the exact statement from the source, so my confidence is moderate.
